Each evaluation is grounded in specific evidence: Q1 answered by the will naming Patrick as 'eldest son'; Q2 addressed by naming census, vital records, probate, church, and naturalization searches with specific outcomes; Q3 justified by the strength of direct evidence; Q4 verified by citing NARA microfilm numbers and FamilySearch access; Q5 confirmed no conflicts exist. The reasoning is defensible and tied to actual log entries (log_001, log_004, log_006, log_007).

dimensions.name: Declaration honesty
dimensions.rationale: The skill resisted premature declaration and applied rigorous criteria. It correctly treated the skipped death certificate as a verified inaccessibility (destroyed in 1920 fire) rather than an unsearched gap, allowing the declaration to proceed. It explicitly named gaps (baptism records fragmentary, naturalization low-value) and justified why they do not block exhaustiveness. The declared=true flag is honest and defensible given the will's direct evidence and the confirmed inaccessibility of the death certificate, not a workaround to make the project appear done.

dimensions.name: Stop criteria coverage
dimensions.rationale: All seven stop criteria keys are present in the stop_criteria object with substantive 1–2 sentence assessments tied to specific evidence: goal_alignment cites the will and census co-enumerations; repository_breadth names FamilySearch, Ancestry, MyHeritage and confirms death certificate inaccessibility; original_substitution cites NARA microfilm numbers; independent_verification describes three distinct institutional sources; evidence_class identifies the will as primary; conflict_resolution states no conflicts; overturn_risk assesses the burden on hypothetical unsearched records. Each assessment is grounded in project state, not generic boilerplate.
